title: Domain of the Gaussian generator
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\bbr^n\to\bbr$. Then $f$ lies in the Gaussian generator domain exactly when there exists a function $g:\bbr^n\to\bbr$ such that both $f$ and $g$ are square-integrable for product standard Gaussian measure and $\bigl(f-P_{e^{-t}}f\bigr)/t$ converges to $g$ in that $L^2$ norm as $t\to0^+$, where $P_{e^{-t}}$ is Gaussian noise with parameter $e^{-t}$.
